raw_response:
I've been farming these 60 mu for 25 years now, since I took over from my father when I was 24. My wife and I do most of the work, but our son works in a factory in Handan and only comes back for wheat harvest, so I hire labor when things get busy. At 60 mu we're bigger than the smallholders in our village, but we're not one of those big business farms either — I still watch every yuan.

This year I'm keeping 40 mu in wheat-maize double crop and 20 mu in cotton. I thought about dropping the cotton because picking is such a headache with labor so tight, but cotton prices were decent last year and I need the cash. The wheat-maize is my safety net — even if one crop disappoints, the other usually pulls through.

For the wheat, I'll plant the first week of October like always. I buy improved seed from the county seed station — about 15 kg per mu, costs me around 35 yuan. I rotary till after the maize residue is chopped, then level the field. For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer as base before planting, about 25 kg per mu. Then at jointing — around Qingming — I topdress with urea, about 15 kg per mu. The extension agent said I could cut back to 12 kg, but I tried that on 5 mu in 2019 and lost nearly 50 kg per mu, so I'm not risking it. Total nitrogen works out to about 18 kg per mu. I irrigate three times: once after planting if it's dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I don't do more because the pump electricity bill adds up fast. I spray herbicide before planting and watch for aphids — if they show up I'll spray insecticide, but I don't do it preventively anymore.

The maize goes in right after wheat harvest in early June. That window is brutal — sometimes less than a week. I hire Old Wang's planter because I don't own one, and I put compound fertilizer in the row at planting, about 20 kg per mu. That's my main nitrogen, around 16 kg per mu total. If the rains are good I might not irrigate at all, but usually I give it one watering when the tassels come out. Last year was dry so I watered twice, but you can't count on that. For labor, it's mostly family for spraying and irrigation, but I hire two days per mu for planting and harvest help.

The cotton is planted in late April. I plow in spring, make beds, and use plastic mulch — it warms the soil and keeps weeds down. I use hybrid seed, about 5 kg per mu. I fertilize twice: base compound fertilizer before mulching, then a side-dress at flowering. Total nitrogen is about 14 kg per mu. Cotton needs more pesticide than grain crops — I spray for bollworm four or five times, and use herbicide under the mulch. I irrigate twice, maybe three times if July is hot. The real problem is picking. My wife and I can handle some, but 20 mu is too much. I hire women from the village and pay by the kilo. It's expensive but there's no other way.

I'm expecting wheat around 450 kg per mu, maize around 500 kg per mu, and cotton around 300 kg per mu of seed cotton. I'm not changing much from last year — fertilizer prices are still high and I need to keep cash in hand in case my son needs help with his wedding expenses. I'd rather apply a bit too much fertilizer than too little. A bad year hurts more than a good year helps.
